gates.reason: 'Never write docs/security-strategy.md without a round-trip parse first; on parse failure output the warnings and do NOT write' is AGENT-orchestrated — the model calls parseSecurityStrategy(), asserts no warnings, and only then calls atomicWriteFileSync. It is a sequence the model performs by following Steps 3-7, not a single CLI whose exit code a cli-exit recipe can assert. (npm run security:refresh runs AFTER the write to sync the index; its secret-classifier REFUSE is a downstream infra behaviour, not this write-gate.)

'Never include real secrets in the markdown' is an authoring constraint the model honours; redactSecrets() is a defence-in-depth backstop in the refresh pipeline, not the gate the SKILL states. Asserting 'the author never typed a secret' is not mechanically checkable from an exit code — it is a judgement about intent no oracle in the closed registry fits.

'Never inflate the threat model — real assets + realistic actors only' is a judgement call about whether a threat is realistic. There is no mechanical oracle for 'is this threat model honest'; it is the archetypal document-only claim.

'The skill is on-demand only — it never blocks /cycle, /plan, or any other skill' is a NEGATIVE cross-skill guarantee. Verifying it would require asserting that no other skill invokes security-strategy as a gate — a source-graph negative with no oracle in the closed registry; the cli-exit oracle cannot assert an absence of invocation.

ignoredCandidates.reason: The worktree-preflight marker block's inlined `skills:hydrate` recipe. Every node one-liner carries `require` and `process.exit`, two ENFORCEMENT_VERBS, and no phrasing of a runnable recipe avoids them — the verbs are JavaScript here, not an enforcement claim about this skill. The recipe is inlined rather than cited because in an unadopted consumer both of the old pointers are dead at once (no `skills:hydrate` script yet, and `docs/runbooks/` is not synced), so a skill file is the only carrier that reaches the reader. Byte-identical across all 16 contracts by construction: it is generated from CONSUMER_HYDRATE_NPM_SCRIPT via MARKER_BLOCK, and `checkSkill` pins the block in every copy.

ignoredCandidates.reason: States a fact about the consumer-sync mechanism (npm scripts are never merged into a consumer's package.json), which is why `--if-present` is needed — not a claim this skill enforces. The flag itself is not a gate: it makes the refresh step a silent no-op when the script is absent, the opposite of enforcement.
